The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 100, Verses 10–11 (Part 1 of 2)

Discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿And that which is in the breasts is brought out (10). Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully aware of them (11).﴾

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. Some of them said: By "the charging, panting ones" is meant the horses that run while neighing.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: the horses. But someone other than Ibn 'Abbas claimed that they are camels.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it refers to fighting.

* Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: the horses.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' informed us, saying: 'Ikrimah was asked about His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. He said: Have you not seen the horse when it runs, how it pants (yadbah)? Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: No animal pants (yadbah) except the dog and the horse.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. He said: the horses pant.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: they are the horses, which run until they pant.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: they are the horses running until they pant.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, like the report of Bishr from Yazid. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, saying: I heard Salim reciting ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, and he said: they are the horses that run panting (dabhan).

* Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: the horses.

* Waki' related to us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: No animal ever panted (dabhat) except a dog or a horse.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: they are the horses.

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to me, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They are the horses.

And others said: They are the camels.

Those who said this:

* Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, who said: They are the camels.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

* 'Isa ibn 'Uthman al-Ramli related to me, saying: my paternal uncle Yahya ibn 'Isa al-Ramli related to me, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, who said: They are the camels when they pant (tanaffasat).

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed us, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who related to him, saying: While I was sitting in al-Hijr, a man came to me asking about ﴿the charging steeds, panting﴾. I said to him: They are the horses when they raid in the way of God; then they take shelter at night, so they prepare their food and kindle their fire. He turned away from me and went to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, while he was under the water-tank of Zamzam, and asked him about ﴿the charging steeds, panting﴾. 'Ali said: Did you ask anyone about it before me? He said: Yes, I asked Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: They are the horses when they raid in the way of God. 'Ali said: Go and call him for me. When I stood over his head, he said: You give legal opinions to people about what you have no knowledge of. By God, the first raid in Islam was Badr, and there were only two horses with us: a horse for al-Zubayr and a horse for al-Miqdad. How then could the charging ones be panting?! Rather, the charging ones, panting, are from 'Arafah to Muzdalifah to Mina. Ibn 'Abbas said: So I retracted my statement and returned to what 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, had said.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, who said: The camels.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: It refers to the Hajj.

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: They are the camels, meaning ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: They are the camels.

The most correct of the two opinions in my view is the view of those who said: By "the charging ones" is meant the horses. This is because camels do not pant; rather, it is the horses that pant. God, may He be exalted, has informed us that they charge panting, and al-Dabh (panting) is what we have already mentioned. And the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, who said: 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The dabh of the horses is the ḥamḥamah (low neighing), and of the camels is the nafs (breathing).

* He said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas describe the dabh: ah ah.

* * *

And His words: ﴿and those that strike sparks with their hooves﴾

The exegetes differed concerning this. Some of them said: They are the horses that strike fire with their hooves.

Those who said this:

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, saying: 'Ikrimah was asked about His words ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾. He said: They struck and produced sparks.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: They are the horses. Al-Kalbi said: They strike with their hooves until fire comes out of them.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata' ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: They produced fire with their hooves.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾: They strike the stones with their hooves.

And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that the horses stir up war between their companions and their riders.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: They stir up war between them and their enemy.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: They stir up war between them and their enemy.

And others said: Rather, what is meant by that are those who kindle fire after they have withdrawn from the battle.

Those who said this:

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, asked me about ﴿By the charging steeds, panting, and those that strike sparks﴾. I said to him: They are the horses that raid in the way of God; then they take shelter at night, so they prepare their food and kindle their fire.

And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the scheming of men.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: The scheming.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: The scheming of men.

And others said: They are the tongues.

Those who said this:

* al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, who said: It is said regarding this verse ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾: They are the tongues.

And others said: They are the camels when they march, scattering pebbles with their soles.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: When they scatter pebbles with their soles, the pebbles strike one another, and fire comes out of them.

The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by "those that strike sparks," the ones that kindle fires by striking. The horses kindle with their hooves; people kindle with the flint; the tongue, for example, kindles with speech; and men kindle with scheming, for example. Likewise, the horses stir up war among its people when they meet in battle. God did not indicate that what is meant is some and not others. So everything that strikes fire by striking is included in what He swore by, because of the generality of that in its apparent sense.

* * *

And His words: ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾

The exegetes differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: The meaning is: those that attack the enemy at dawn openly.

Those who said this:

* 29259 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man asked me about "those that attack at dawn," and he said: They are the horses that raid in the way of God.

* 29260 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' informed us, saying: I asked 'Ikrimah about His words ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾, and he said: They attacked the enemy at dawn.

* 29261 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾, who said: They are the horses.

* 29262 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾, who said: They are the horses.

* 29263 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾, who said: The people raided after they had reached morning against their enemy.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾, who said: They raided when they had reached morning.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾, who said: The people raided when they had reached morning.

And others said: What is meant by it is the camels when they are pushed by their riders from Jam' on the day of sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) to Mina.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿and those that attack at dawn﴾: when they pour out from Jam'.

The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, swore by "those that attack at dawn," and He did not single out one attacker over another. So every attacker at dawn is included in what He swore by. Zayd ibn Aslam used to mention the explanation of these letters and reject it, saying: It is only an oath that God swore by.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting, and those that strike sparks﴾: This is an oath God swore by. And regarding His words ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: All this is an oath. He said: My father did not look into it when he was asked about it, nor did he mention it, meaning by it the oath.

* * *

And His words ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then they raise dust in the valley; al-naq' is dust, and it is said that it is earth. The pronoun in His words "therewith" (bihi) refers to a place, and it was not mentioned earlier, because it is known that dust is not raised except from a place; so the hearers' understanding of its meaning dispenses with mentioning it.

The exegetes said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: The horses.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata' and Ibn Zayd, who said: al-Naq' is dust.

* Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: They raised dust, meaning the horses.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, saying: 'Ikrimah was asked about His words ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, and he said: They raised the earth with their hooves.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: They raised dust of the earth with their hooves.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: They raised dust therewith.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Ali said to me: Rather, the charging ones, panting, are from 'Arafah to Muzdalifah, and from Muzdalifah to Mina. ﴿Then raise therewith dust﴾: the earth when they trample it with their hooves and soles.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: When they march they raise dust.

* * *

And His words: ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then they penetrate with their riders into the midst of the people. It is said: wasatt al-qawm (I penetrated the people) with the light form, and wassatuhu (I put him in the middle) with the intensive form, and tawassatuhu (I got into the middle of him) with the same meaning.

The exegetes said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, who said: 'Ikrimah was asked about His words ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, and he said: The host of the disbelievers.

* Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: The host of the people.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: It is the host of the people.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata' ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: The host of the enemy.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: The host of these and those.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: they penetrate the midst of the people's host.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: they penetrate the people with the host of the enemy.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: They penetrated the midst of the people's host.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: al-Jam' is the battalion (katibah).

And others said: Rather, what is meant by ﴿then penetrate therewith﴾ is Muzdalifah.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, meaning: Muzdalifah.

* * *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾

He says: Indeed man is ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord. The land al-kanud is that which produces nothing. Al-A'sha said:

Make a new beginning with her, she will make a new beginning for your union,
For indeed she is barren (kunud) for the union of the frequent visitor.[[Tarajimat al-Qur'an: plural of tarjuman, and he meant the exegetes; see what has passed: 70, note: 1.]]

It is also said: Kindah was so named because it cut off its father.

The exegetes said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Ubayd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, saying: Muslim related to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾: He said: ungrateful (kafur).

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 100, verses 10–11 (part 2 of 2)**

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "To his Lord, ungrateful (kafur)."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "Ungrateful (kafur)."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Mahdi ibn Maymun, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab, from al-Hasan al-Basri: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "He is the ungrateful one who counts (i.e., dwells on) calamities and forgets the blessings of his Lord."

⁕ Waki' related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', who said: "al-Kanud: al-kafur (the ungrateful)."

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And indeed mankind is, in love of wealth, intense.

The grammarians of Arabic (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding the basis for describing him with intensity in his love of wealth. Some of the Basran grammarians said: The meaning of that is: "And indeed he, because of his love of good, is intense," that is, stingy (bakhil). They said: The stingy person is called "shadid" (intense) and "mutashaddid" (tight-fisted). They cited as evidence for this the verse of Tarafah ibn al-'Abd al-Bakri:

I see death seizing souls and choosing
The precious wealth of the stingy, tight-fisted one [[Hadith 174. Its isnad is very weak. Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi: trustworthy; al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Khuzaymah and others related from him. He died in 258 AH, and is biographed in al-Tahdhib. Some have spoken about the narration of some of them, but the truth is that he is trustworthy, and Muslim narrated from him in his Sahih. The nephew of al-Harith al-A'war: even more unknown than that; neither he nor his father is named. His paternal uncle al-Harith: he is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'war al-Hamdani, and he is very weak. The scholars differed about him greatly, to the point that al-Sha'bi and others described him as "a liar." I have already concluded in the commentary on hadith 565 and elsewhere in the Musnad that he is very weak.

As for the text of the hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim related it in meaning, from al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, with this isnad, as Ibn Kathir transmitted it (1:50), though the isnad was distorted there. It is part of a long hadith on the virtues of the Qur'an, related by al-Tirmidhi (4:51–52 in Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi), from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Husayn al-Ju'fi, with this isnad. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Hamzah al-Zayyat, and its isnad is unknown (majhul), and there is criticism of the hadith of al-Harith." Likewise al-Darimi related it in his Sunan (2:435), from Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Rifa'i, from Husayn al-Ju'fi. al-Suyuti transmitted it (1:15) and attributed it also to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. al-Dhahabi alluded to it in al-Mizan (3:380), in the biography of Abu al-Mukhtar al-Ta'i, saying: "His hadith on the virtues of the Qur'an is munkar (rejected)." Ibn Kathir transmitted it in al-Fada'il (pp. 14–15) from al-Tirmidhi and related his weakening of it, then said: "Hamzah ibn Habib al-Zayyat did not single it out in narration; rather Muhammad ibn Ishaq related it from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi from al-Harith al-A'war. Thus Hamzah is cleared of its burden. Yet although he is weak in hadith, he is an imam in recitation. The hadith is well known from the narration of al-Harith al-A'war, and they have spoken about it; indeed some of them accused him of lying in respect of his opinion and belief, but as for deliberately lying in hadith, no. The essence of this hadith is that it may be a statement of the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and some have erred in attributing it to the Prophet; it is a good and sound statement."

Two further isnads, with the same content, will come at 175 and 176 as mawquf (stopping at the Companion), from the statement of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

The narration of Ibn Ishaq, to which Ibn Kathir alluded, is the hadith of Ahmad in the Musnad (565), from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq. We have already weakened its isnad there, due to al-Harith al-A'war and its discontinuity between Ibn Ishaq and Muhammad ibn Ka'b. And it does not contain the phrase found here, in the "Sirat al-Mustaqim" (the Straight Path) commentary.]]

Others said: Its meaning is: "And indeed he, in love of good, is strong."

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: The position of ﴿li-hubbi﴾ (in love of) should have been after "shadid" (intense), and "shadid" should have been made to take it as its complement, so that the statement would be: "And indeed he is intense in love of good." But since the love was mentioned first in the speech, it was said "shadid," and its final part was omitted because its mention came earlier, and for the sake of the verse endings (ru'us al-ayat). He said: A similar case is in Surah Ibrahim: ﴿like ashes which the wind blew hard against on a stormy day﴾. Stormy-ness (al-'usuf) does not belong to a day; it belongs only to the wind. So when the mention of the wind came before the day, the last word was dropped, as if he said: "on a stormy day of wind," and Allah knows best.

Those of ta'wil said the like of what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of good, intense﴾: "The good is the world." And he recited: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth (khayran), the bequest﴾. He (the narrator) said: I said to him: "﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾: does that mean property?" He said: "Yes, and what else is it but property?" He said: "It may be unlawful, but people call it good, so Allah named it good, because people call it good in this world. It may be wicked, and fighting in the cause of Allah was called evil (su'), and he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty; no harm (su') touched them﴾." He said: "No harm touched them, meaning no fighting touched them. And it is not evil in the sight of Allah, but they call it evil."

The meaning of the statement is: Indeed mankind is ungrateful to his Lord, and indeed he is intense in love of good, and indeed Allah, concerning that of His command, is a witness. But His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾ has been placed earlier, and its meaning is delayed; it was made a parenthetical insertion between His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾ and His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense﴾.

Those of ta'wil said the like of what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful, and indeed he is, to that, a witness﴾. He said: "This is in the forward placement of speech." He said: "It means: Indeed Allah is a witness that mankind is intense in love of good."

As for His saying: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered﴾.

He says: Does not this human being, who has this description, know that when what is in the graves is stirred up, and the dead within them are brought out and examined?

It is mentioned that in the codex of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "when what is in the graves is examined (bahatha)," and the people of ta'wil interpreted it likewise.

Those who said that:

He says: Indeed their Lord, regarding their deeds, and what they concealed in their breasts and kept hidden within them, and what they made public by their limbs, knows, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for all of that on that Day.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 100, Verses 10–11 (Part 1 of 2)

Discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿And that which is in the breasts is brought out (10). Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully aware of them (11).﴾

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. Some of them said: By "the charging, panting ones" is meant the horses that run while neighing.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: the horses. He said: Have you not seen the horse when it runs, how it pants (yadbah)? Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: No animal pants (yadbah) except the dog and the horse.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾. He said: the horses pant.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: they are the horses, which run until they pant.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: they are the horses running until they pant.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, saying: I heard Salim reciting ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, and he said: they are the horses that run panting (dabhan).

* Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾: He said: the horses.

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to me, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They are the horses.

And others said: They are the camels.

Those who said this:

* Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, who said: They are the camels.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

When I stood over his head, he said: You give legal opinions to people about what you have no knowledge of. By God, the first raid in Islam was Badr, and there were only two horses with us: a horse for al-Zubayr and a horse for al-Miqdad. How then could the charging ones be panting?! He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: It refers to the Hajj.

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: They are the camels, meaning ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ﴿By the charging steeds, panting﴾, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: They are the camels.

The most correct of the two opinions in my view is the view of those who said: By "the charging ones" is meant the horses. This is because camels do not pant; rather, it is the horses that pant. God, may He be exalted, has informed us that they charge panting, and al-Dabh (panting) is what we have already mentioned. And the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said regarding this.

* Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, who said: 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The dabh of the horses is the ḥamḥamah (low neighing), and of the camels is the nafs (breathing).

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: The scheming.

Those who said this:

* al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, who said: It is said regarding this verse ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾: They are the tongues.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿and those that strike sparks﴾, who said: When they scatter pebbles with their soles, the pebbles strike one another, and fire comes out of them.

The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by "those that strike sparks," the ones that kindle fires by striking. Likewise, the horses stir up war among its people when they meet in battle. God did not indicate that what is meant is some and not others. So everything that strikes fire by striking is included in what He swore by, because of the generality of that in its apparent sense.

The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, swore by "those that attack at dawn," and He did not single out one attacker over another. So every attacker at dawn is included in what He swore by. Zayd ibn Aslam used to mention the explanation of these letters and reject it, saying: It is only an oath that God swore by.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿By the charging steeds, panting, and those that strike sparks﴾: This is an oath God swore by. And regarding His words ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: All this is an oath. He said: My father did not look into it when he was asked about it, nor did he mention it, meaning by it the oath.

* * *

And His words ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then they raise dust in the valley; al-naq' is dust, and it is said that it is earth. The pronoun in His words "therewith" (bihi) refers to a place, and it was not mentioned earlier, because it is known that dust is not raised except from a place; so the hearers' understanding of its meaning dispenses with mentioning it.

The exegetes said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: The horses.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata' and Ibn Zayd, who said: al-Naq' is dust.

* Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: They raised dust, meaning the horses.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, saying: 'Ikrimah was asked about His words ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, and he said: They raised the earth with their hooves.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: They raised dust of the earth with their hooves.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: They raised dust therewith.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Ali said to me: Rather, the charging ones, panting, are from 'Arafah to Muzdalifah, and from Muzdalifah to Mina. ﴿Then raise therewith dust﴾: the earth when they trample it with their hooves and soles.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿then raise therewith dust﴾, who said: When they march they raise dust.

* * *

And His words: ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then they penetrate with their riders into the midst of the people. It is said: wasatt al-qawm (I penetrated the people) with the light form, and wassatuhu (I put him in the middle) with the intensive form, and tawassatuhu (I got into the middle of him) with the same meaning.

The exegetes said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, who said: 'Ikrimah was asked about His words ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, and he said: The host of the disbelievers.

* Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: The host of the people.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: It is the host of the people.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata' ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: The host of the enemy.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: The host of these and those.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: they penetrate the midst of the people's host.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: they penetrate the people with the host of the enemy.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, who said: They penetrated the midst of the people's host.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾: al-Jam' is the battalion (katibah).

And others said: Rather, what is meant by ﴿then penetrate therewith﴾ is Muzdalifah.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah ﴿then penetrate therewith into the midst of the host﴾, meaning: Muzdalifah.

* * *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾

He says: Indeed man is ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord. The land al-kanud is that which produces nothing. Al-A'sha said:

Make a new beginning with her, she will make a new beginning for your union,
For indeed she is barren (kunud) for the union of the frequent visitor.[[Tarajimat al-Qur'an: plural of tarjuman, and he meant the exegetes; see what has passed: 70, note: 1.]]

It is also said: Kindah was so named because it cut off its father.

The exegetes said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Ubayd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, saying: Muslim related to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾: He said: ungrateful (kafur).

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 100, verses 10–11 (part 2 of 2)**

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "To his Lord, ungrateful (kafur)."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "Ungrateful (kafur)."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Mahdi ibn Maymun, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab, from al-Hasan al-Basri: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "He is the ungrateful one who counts (i.e., dwells on) calamities and forgets the blessings of his Lord."

⁕ Waki' related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', who said: "al-Kanud: al-kafur (the ungrateful)."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, who said: al-Hasan said: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾, meaning: "Lawwam (one who blames) to his Lord, who counts calamities."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿ungrateful﴾. He said: "Kafur (ungrateful)."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "Kafur (ungrateful)."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, the like of it.

⁕ Yahya ibn Habib ibn 'Arabi related to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Simak, that he said: "Kindah was only named so because it severed its father (qata'at abahu)." ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. He said: "Kafur (ungrateful)."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Isra'il, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾, and said: "The ungrateful (kafur) is the one who eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds his gift (rifd)."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾: "al-Kanud: al-kafur." And he recited: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash related to us, saying: Abu al-Mughirah 'Abd al-Quddus related to us, saying: Huraiz ibn 'Uthman related to us, saying: Hamzah ibn Hani' related to me, from Abu Umamah, that he used to say: "al-Kanud is the one who eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds his gift."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sawwari related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar related to us, saying: Abu al-Yaqzan informed us, from Sufyan, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾: "Lawwam to his Lord, who counts calamities and forgets blessings."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed Allah is a witness to his ungratefulness toward his Lord; that is, a witness (shahid).

Those of ta'wil (the interpreters, ahl al-ta'wil) said the like of what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾. He said: "He says: Indeed Allah is a witness to that."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾. In some readings: "Indeed Allah is a witness to that."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾. He said: "And indeed Allah is a witness against him."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And indeed mankind is, in love of wealth, intense.

The grammarians of Arabic (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding the basis for describing him with intensity in his love of wealth. Some of the Basran grammarians said: The meaning of that is: "And indeed he, because of his love of good, is intense," that is, stingy (bakhil). They said: The stingy person is called "shadid" (intense) and "mutashaddid" (tight-fisted). They cited as evidence for this the verse of Tarafah ibn al-'Abd al-Bakri:

I see death seizing souls and choosing
The precious wealth of the stingy, tight-fisted one [[Hadith 174. Its isnad is very weak. Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi: trustworthy; al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Khuzaymah and others related from him. He died in 258 AH, and is biographed in al-Tahdhib. Husayn al-Ju'fi: he is Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn al-Walid, a well-known trustworthy narrator, related from by Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and others; indeed Ibn 'Uyaynah related from him although he was older than him. The authors of the six canonical books narrated from him. Hamzah al-Zayyat: he is Hamzah ibn Habib, the well-known reciter. Some have spoken about the narration of some of them, but the truth is that he is trustworthy, and Muslim narrated from him in his Sahih. Abu al-Mukhtar al-Ta'i: it is said his name is Sa'd; he is unknown (majhul), al-Madini and Abu Zur'ah considered him unknown. The nephew of al-Harith al-A'war: even more unknown than that; neither he nor his father is named. His paternal uncle al-Harith: he is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'war al-Hamdani, and he is very weak. The scholars differed about him greatly, to the point that al-Sha'bi and others described him as "a liar." I have already concluded in the commentary on hadith 565 and elsewhere in the Musnad that he is very weak.

As for the text of the hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim related it in meaning, from al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, with this isnad, as Ibn Kathir transmitted it (1:50), though the isnad was distorted there. It is part of a long hadith on the virtues of the Qur'an, related by al-Tirmidhi (4:51–52 in Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi), from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Husayn al-Ju'fi, with this isnad. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Hamzah al-Zayyat, and its isnad is unknown (majhul), and there is criticism of the hadith of al-Harith." Likewise al-Darimi related it in his Sunan (2:435), from Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Rifa'i, from Husayn al-Ju'fi. al-Suyuti transmitted it (1:15) and attributed it also to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. al-Dhahabi alluded to it in al-Mizan (3:380), in the biography of Abu al-Mukhtar al-Ta'i, saying: "His hadith on the virtues of the Qur'an is munkar (rejected)." Ibn Kathir transmitted it in al-Fada'il (pp. 14–15) from al-Tirmidhi and related his weakening of it, then said: "Hamzah ibn Habib al-Zayyat did not single it out in narration; rather Muhammad ibn Ishaq related it from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi from al-Harith al-A'war. Thus Hamzah is cleared of its burden. Yet although he is weak in hadith, he is an imam in recitation. The hadith is well known from the narration of al-Harith al-A'war, and they have spoken about it; indeed some of them accused him of lying in respect of his opinion and belief, but as for deliberately lying in hadith, no. The essence of this hadith is that it may be a statement of the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and some have erred in attributing it to the Prophet; it is a good and sound statement."

Two further isnads, with the same content, will come at 175 and 176 as mawquf (stopping at the Companion), from the statement of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

The narration of Ibn Ishaq, to which Ibn Kathir alluded, is the hadith of Ahmad in the Musnad (565), from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq. We have already weakened its isnad there, due to al-Harith al-A'war and its discontinuity between Ibn Ishaq and Muhammad ibn Ka'b. And it does not contain the phrase found here, in the "Sirat al-Mustaqim" (the Straight Path) commentary.]]

Others said: Its meaning is: "And indeed he, in love of good, is strong."

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: The position of ﴿li-hubbi﴾ (in love of) should have been after "shadid" (intense), and "shadid" should have been made to take it as its complement, so that the statement would be: "And indeed he is intense in love of good." But since the love was mentioned first in the speech, it was said "shadid," and its final part was omitted because its mention came earlier, and for the sake of the verse endings (ru'us al-ayat). He said: A similar case is in Surah Ibrahim: ﴿like ashes which the wind blew hard against on a stormy day﴾. Stormy-ness (al-'usuf) does not belong to a day; it belongs only to the wind. So when the mention of the wind came before the day, the last word was dropped, as if he said: "on a stormy day of wind," and Allah knows best.

Those of ta'wil said the like of what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of good, intense﴾: "The good is the world." And he recited: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth (khayran), the bequest﴾. He (the narrator) said: I said to him: "﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾: does that mean property?" He said: "Yes, and what else is it but property?" He said: "It may be unlawful, but people call it good, so Allah named it good, because people call it good in this world. It may be wicked, and fighting in the cause of Allah was called evil (su'), and he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty; no harm (su') touched them﴾." He said: "No harm touched them, meaning no fighting touched them. And it is not evil in the sight of Allah, but they call it evil."

The meaning of the statement is: Indeed mankind is ungrateful to his Lord, and indeed he is intense in love of good, and indeed Allah, concerning that of His command, is a witness. But His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾ has been placed earlier, and its meaning is delayed; it was made a parenthetical insertion between His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾ and His saying: ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense﴾.

Those of ta'wil said the like of what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful, and indeed he is, to that, a witness﴾. He said: "This is in the forward placement of speech." He said: "It means: Indeed Allah is a witness that mankind is intense in love of good."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered﴾.

He says: Does not this human being, who has this description, know that when what is in the graves is stirred up, and the dead within them are brought out and examined?

It is mentioned that in the codex of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "when what is in the graves is examined (bahatha)," and the people of ta'wil interpreted it likewise.

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿what is in the graves is scattered﴾: "examined." The Arabs have two dialects for (bu'thira): they say "ba'thara" and "bahthara," and both have one meaning.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what is in the breasts is obtained﴾.

He says: It is distinguished and separated, so what is in the breasts of people of good and evil is brought forth.

Those of ta'wil said the like of what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿And what is in the breasts is obtained﴾: "brought forth."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And what is in the breasts is obtained﴾: "distinguished."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, their Lord, concerning them, that Day, is Acquainted﴾.

He says: Indeed their Lord, regarding their deeds, and what they concealed in their breasts and kept hidden within them, and what they made public by their limbs, knows, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for all of that on that Day.
